sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203], while operating income grew faster at 12.3% [F204] and net income at 14.7% [F205].
The window is a steady compounder rather than a cycle: growth ran 7.9% to 9.7% in FY2018-FY2020 [D42][D91][D140], then stepped up to 17.5% in FY2021 [D189] and 15.8% in FY2022 [D238].
FY2021's jump came from a 16% comparable sales increase, strong non-foods and e-commerce, plus gasoline and currency tailwinds [P56][P55].
FY2022 added $30.7 billion of net sales on 14% comparable sales, with gasoline, business centers and travel strongest and inflation running above prior years [P42].
Growth then cooled to 6.8% in FY2023 [D287] and 5.0% in FY2024 [D336] before re-accelerating to 8.2% in FY2025 [D385] and 10.1% in FY2026 [D434].
The US segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue [D670] and 7.2pp of growth [D672], with Other International adding 1.6pp [D679] and Canada 1.3pp [D686].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, of which comparable sales were $22.5 billion, split 5% average ticket and 3% shopping frequency, with the rest from 25 net new warehouses [P14].

Food and Sundries remains the largest product line at 38.5% of revenue [D558] but contributed only 2.6pp of FY2026 growth [D560], while warehouse ancillary and other businesses contributed 3.7pp [D601] on 19.9% growth [D600].
Membership fees are 1.9% of revenue [D663] yet grew 11.0% [D664], and the filing attributes that to new sign-ups, fee increases and Executive upgrades [P13].

Operating income grew 12.5% against 10.1% revenue growth in FY2026 [D435][D434], an incremental margin of 4.7% [D457], and diluted EPS growth of 14.0% [D438] matched net income growth of 13.9% [D436] because the share count was flat [D452].
Operating margin reached 3.9% in FY2026 [F32], its window high [D691] and above the 3.4% median [D692], though it sits in the 17th percentile of retail peers against a 5.0% median [D709][D710].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp [D447], with SG&A adding 0.1pp [D460] and cost of revenue flat [D459]; SG&A fell to 9.0% of revenue from 9.1% [D414][D365].
The filing attributes the 10bp SG&A decline to sales leverage, noting SG&A excluding gasoline inflation was 9.26%, up one basis point, and currency added $126 million of expense [P9].
Gross margin fell three basis points, with IEEPA tariff refunds adding three basis points and mix shifting toward faster-growing ancillary businesses [P12].
Net margin of 3.0% [F52] trails operating margin by 0.8pp [D732], reflecting a 24.7% effective tax rate [D420] and modest interest expense of $145 million [X70].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income in FY2026 [F82][F42][D421], near the 1.75x window median [D722], and free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x net income [F102][D422].
The 18.6% operating cash flow increase came from higher operating income and a reduced net inventory investment on faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [D439][P6].
Free cash flow margin was 3.1% [D418], above the 2.8% median [D698] but below the 4.2% retail peer median [D714], with capex at 2.1% of revenue [D417] and 2.41x D&A [D423].
Investing outflow rose to $6.4 billion from $5.3 billion, primarily capital expenditures [F112][F111][P5].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion in FY2026 [D427], 5.0% of revenue [D428], the 100th percentile of four retail peers against a -18.3% median [D733][D734].
Cash and investments rose 39.4% to $21.3 billion [D453][D425] while total debt grew 6.5% to $6.2 billion [D454][D426], and the current ratio was 1.06x [F182].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.3 billion were 35.2% of free cash flow [D429][D430], including $848 million of repurchases [X110] and $2.5 billion of dividends [X120].
The $4.0 billion repurchase authorization had $1.1 billion remaining at FY2026 end, and repurchased shares are retired [P3].
No red-flag candidates were supplied in the pack, so the screen covered margin compression, cash conversion, leverage and dilution and none triggered.

The one soft spot is relative profitability: operating margin sits in the 17th percentile of six retail peers [D709] and net margin likewise [D711], a structural feature of the membership model rather than a deterioration.
Free cash flow conversion has been volatile, ranging from 0.60x net income in FY2022 [D699] to 1.58x in FY2017 [D700], so a single year's 1.02x [D422] is not a durable signal.
Operating margin: a print below the 3.4% window median [D692] in the FY2027 10-K would reverse the FY2024-FY2026 climb from 3.6% to 3.9% [F30][F32].
Free cash flow margin: holding at or above the 2.8% median [D698] would confirm the FY2026 level of 3.1% [D418] as the new base rather than a peak.
Membership fee growth: a deceleration below the FY2026 rate of 11.0% [D664] would undercut the fee-increase benefit the FY2024 filing expected to add roughly $370 million over two years [P25].
